$description: #271 harvest lane C — page-frame + page-title + wayfinding + arrangement. Every source consulted. Ours = file/path in this repo. External = URL + VERBATIM quote (<15 words), marked EXTERNAL, per knowledge/_RUNBOOK-external-claims.md. NOTHING HERE IS OUR RULE until Dave rules it.
$read_only: This lane touched NOTHING under knowledge/. No meta, schema, roles.json, rules index or gate was written.

ours.said: 7 shells, every one with a when: top-nav 'default for dashboards'; side-nav '> 7 destinations or two nav levels'; nav-rail 'dense app, content cannot spare 248px'; multi-column 'list-and-detail job'; split 'two peers on screen at once'; focused 'one job, no navigation (auth, wizard)'; doormat 'marketing / servicing site with a mega-footer'
ours.note: ADOPTED s252-D1. CANON. Axis is destination COUNT + job, not device size.

ours.said: page-header-lockup 'page level, with actions or tabs'; headers 'page or screen level, app-only, no lock-up needed'; section-heading-lockup 'section level, above one board / table / panel'; eyebrow 'a kicker alone is enough (rare)'
ours.note: CANON s252-D1. The axis is LEVEL.

ours.said: navigations 'global'; sidebar-nav 'global, desktop, persistent column'; tabs 'local — peer views in one context'; breadcrumbs 'ancestry, depth >= 2'; anchor-nav 'in-page, long document'; tab-bar 'mobile bottom, 3–5 destinations'; pagination 'within one list'; back-to-top 'page chrome only'
ours.note: CANON s252-D1. Only tab-bar carries a NUMBER; breadcrumbs carries a DEPTH.

ours.said: layout-utilities 'default'; cards 'a bordered surface per item'; stats-band-lockup '3–6 headline-metrics in a labelled row'; feature-grid-lockup 'marketing, 2/3/4-up icon + title + body'; splitter 'the reader sizes two panes'; accordion 'content collapses behind a heading'; carousel 'one of a set at a time'; divider 'a rule alone'
ours.note: CANON s252-D1. divider / splitter / layout-utilities / feature-grid-lockup are slice C; accordion / carousel / cards are slice B's components.

ours.said: destinations <= 7 AND nav.levels <= 2 — the default for dashboards — beats app-shell-side-nav ('> 7 destinations or two nav levels') below those bounds
ours.note: ONE of only five metas in this slice that already carries a machine-shaped when.

ours.said: level in (page, screen, section) AND platform = app AND lockup = none — yields to page-header-lockup whenever actions or tabs ride the band
shape = destination-set x links AND scope = global — beats breadcrumbs and tabs because those are ancestry and local peers, not the global set
shape = ancestor-path x links AND depth >= 2
ours.note: OUR NUMBER IS 2. Two external systems say 3. See DECISION-TABLE R3.

ours.said: content = arbitrary-blocks AND surface = none — beats cards whenever the arrangement must paint nothing
A permanent 64px icon rail. It is not App-shell-side-nav's collapsed state — there is no expand toggle, and that absence is the component
ours.note: our discriminator is the ABSENCE of a toggle; no external system draws that line.

ours.said: the only shell in the library defined by what it REMOVES — no primary navigation, no breadcrumb, no utility group, no search
Never repeat the masthead's destinations in the mat. A doormat that duplicates the masthead is a doormat that has stopped being read
ours.note: USWDS says the same thing in its own words — see external[46].

ours.said: Never put a mega-footer on an authenticated task screen. That is App-shell-focused's territory
App-level BOTTOM navigation: 3–5 equal-width destinations. NOT the in-page Tabs component
ours.note: 3–5 is OUR number and it is already in roles.json.

ours.said: Use it on long single-page content (product terms, rates and fees)
ours.note: 'long' carries no threshold. USWDS supplies one — see DECISION-TABLE R9.

ours.said: Use it where two things must stay on screen together and the right balance between them is the reader's business, not the layout's
Its question is 'what is THIS, and what happened to it?' — one record, in depth, which is what separates it from the dashboard
ours.note: the template family discriminates by QUESTION ASKED. That axis has no external equivalent — no public system ships page templates at this granularity.

ours.said: A dashboard answers 'how are things right now'; a report is A CLAIM ABOUT A PERIOD, made at a MOMENT, from a stated SOURCE
It answers the same question as Template dashboard and differs in ONE thing: its layout
ours.note: ⛔ the two dashboards are NOT discriminated by job. Only by grammar. Dave's call.

ours.said: IT DRAWS BOTH BODIES — a Data-grid table AND a Document-row list — because the library holds both answers and they are NOT interchangeable
ours.note: defers to slice B's table-vs-list-items rule.

ours.said: A large, responsive marketing banner at the top of a page, carrying a primary message (headline + intro + CTA)
ours.note: MARKETING vs APPLICATION is the real cut and no meta states it as a predicate.

ours.said: The APP FOOTER: the contentinfo landmark at the bottom of an authenticated application's content column
ours.note: our Footer is the OPERATOR footer (build, environment, freshness). USWDS/GOV.UK footers are the SITE footer. Different objects with the same name.

ours.said: an eyebrow/breadcrumb, the page title, an optional Tabs row and a right-aligned action pair
ours.note: it CARRIES a Tabs row — three external systems say tabs are never navigation. See DECISION-TABLE R11.

ours.said: the repeatable in-page heading that sits above one section of content — as distinct from Page-header-lockup's page-level h1
N cells of icon + title + body, arranged 2/3/4-up (its per-cell action-button row deliberately omitted)
The from/to account picker of every payment flow plus its compact inline token
ours.note: DOMAIN component. No public system ships it; nothing external to harvest.

ours.said: #270 proposed whens for the selection and record-list families, and s270-D1 (single-select cut-off 5, provisional)
ours.note: REFERENCED, NOT REDONE, per BRIEF rule.
